evidence.claim: The Bundestag elects the chancellor by absolute majority, and removal is only possible through a constructive vote of no confidence that also names a successor.
evidence.title: Election of the Federal Chancellor
evidence.excerpt: The Bundestag elects the chancellor by absolute majority, and removal is only possible through a constructive vote of no confidence that also names a successor.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official parliamentary procedure page; strong for constraints on chancellor power.
evidence.period_fit: Directly relevant to Scholz's coalition-dependent authority in 2022.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Structural constraint on Scholz's governing power rather than a personal act.
contrary_evidence: Describes formal removal mechanics, not informal coalition discipline.
Does not address emergency decision-making inside NATO.

evidence.claim: The cabinet adopted the 2022 supplementary budget and the 2023 budget framework, said fiscal policy was shifting back to stability, promised respect for the debt brake, and expanded future investment in climate, mobility, digitalization, innovation, education, research, and infrastructure.
evidence.title: Staatsfinanzen stabilisieren, Zukunftsinvestitionen ausbauen, fiskalische Resilienz stärken
evidence.excerpt: The cabinet adopted the 2022 supplementary budget and the 2023 budget framework, said fiscal policy was shifting back to stability, promised respect for the debt brake, and expanded future investment in climate, mobility, digitalization, innovation, education, research, and infrastructure.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct ministry budget press release with a dated cabinet decision and explicit fiscal priorities.
evidence.period_fit: Exactly within 2022 and directly relevant to Scholz's fiscal stewardship.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Cabinet-level policy under Scholz; attributable to his government, though implementation depended on parliament and ministries.
contrary_evidence: It was a draft budget, not final spending, and it still relied on extraordinary crisis-era financing assumptions.

evidence.claim: The federal government announced a shield for war-affected companies, including temporary gas and electricity cost damping, KfW-backed credit lines of up to 100 billion euro, and possible equity or hybrid-capital support for especially relevant firms.
evidence.title: Schutzschild der Bundesregierung für vom Krieg betroffene Unternehmen
evidence.excerpt: The federal government announced a shield for war-affected companies, including temporary gas and electricity cost damping, KfW-backed credit lines of up to 100 billion euro, and possible equity or hybrid-capital support for especially relevant firms.
evidence.source_locator: bullet list in the press release summary
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official ministry release with concrete financing figures and policy design.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Government-level economic crisis response under Scholz, with implementation shared across coalition ministries and agencies.
contrary_evidence: Emergency support of this sort can distort competition and increase fiscal risk.

evidence.claim: The cabinet approved gas, electricity, and heat price brakes as the core of the 200 billion euro defense shield, with caps for households and firms and application from March 2023 with January-February retroactive relief.
evidence.title: Bundeskabinett verabschiedet Gas- und Strompreisbremse – Wichtige Entlastung für Verbraucherinnen und Verbraucher und die Wirtschaft
evidence.excerpt: The cabinet approved gas, electricity, and heat price brakes as the core of the 200 billion euro defense shield, with caps for households and firms and application from March 2023 with January-February retroactive relief.
evidence.source_locator: press release introduction and policy description
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official cabinet decision notice with detailed policy parameters and timing.
evidence.period_fit: Exactly within 2022, though the measures took effect mainly in 2023.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Cabinet-level decision under Scholz, with joint drafting by the Chancellery, Finance Ministry, and Economics Ministry.
contrary_evidence: The price brakes were temporary and highly costly, so they are relief rather than structural reform.

evidence.claim: The ministry's table summarized the relief packages as including EEG-levy abolition, fuel-tax cuts, a 350 euro heating subsidy for some housing-benefit recipients, the 300 euro energy allowance, the 100 euro child bonus, a 200 euro payment for some social-benefit recipients, a 100 euro payment for some unemployment-benefit recipients, and the 9 euro public-transport ticket.
evidence.title: Leistungen der Entlastungspakete
evidence.excerpt: The ministry's table summarized the relief packages as including EEG-levy abolition, fuel-tax cuts, a 350 euro heating subsidy for some housing-benefit recipients, the 300 euro energy allowance, the 100 euro child bonus, a 200 euro payment for some social-benefit recipients, a 100 euro payment for some unemployment-benefit recipients, and the 9 euro public-transport ticket.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official ministry summary table with explicit benefit amounts and recipient groups.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Coalition-level crisis relief under Scholz; the table is descriptive rather than a personal statement.
contrary_evidence: These were temporary shock absorbers rather than long-run productivity reforms.

evidence.claim: The Bundestag passed the government's Bürgergeld bill in November 2022; the debate centered on higher standard rates, qualification, bureaucracy reduction, and whether the reform truly overcame poverty and Hartz IV.
evidence.title: Bürgergeld-Gesetz (Regelbedarfsstufen)
evidence.excerpt: The Bundestag passed the government's Bürgergeld bill in November 2022; the debate centered on higher standard rates, qualification, bureaucracy reduction, and whether the reform truly overcame poverty and Hartz IV.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official parliamentary vote record and debate summary for a government bill.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Scholz-government legislation, though enacted through parliamentary coalition bargaining.
contrary_evidence: Opponents argued the reform still left people in poverty and did not fully replace Hartz IV's coercive logic.

evidence.claim: The IMF said Germany's economy showed resilience after the 2022 Russian gas shut-off, that the energy shock and tight financial conditions weighed on growth, and that the authorities' policy response to spillovers from Russia's war in Ukraine was timely and generally well designed.
evidence.title: Germany: 2023 Article IV Consultation-Press Release; Staff Report; and Statement for Germany
evidence.excerpt: The IMF said Germany's economy showed resilience after the 2022 Russian gas shut-off, that the energy shock and tight financial conditions weighed on growth, and that the authorities' policy response to spillovers from Russia's war in Ukraine was timely and generally well designed.
evidence.source_locator: summary and staff appraisal lines 265-267 and 268
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Independent IMF consultation report with explicit evaluation of policy response and macro effects.
evidence.period_fit: Directly reviews the 2022 shock and the government's response.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Assessment of the Scholz government's fiscal and crisis-management response, not personal authorship alone.
contrary_evidence: The IMF also says growth was expected to stay slightly negative in 2023 and that uncertainty remained unusually high.

evidence.claim: Destatis reported annual CPI inflation of 7.9 percent in 2022, with the surge driven primarily by extreme increases in energy and food prices after the start of the war in Ukraine.
evidence.title: Inflationsrate im Jahr 2022 bei +7,9 %
evidence.excerpt: Destatis reported annual CPI inflation of 7.9 percent in 2022, with the surge driven primarily by extreme increases in energy and food prices after the start of the war in Ukraine.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official statistics release with precise annual inflation and stated driver analysis.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Outcome context rather than a direct ruler act, but crucial for judging the government's crisis response.
contrary_evidence: High inflation is a negative macro outcome and not something Scholz fully controlled.

evidence.claim: The 2022 federal structural net borrowing reached 8.09 percent of GDP, exceeding the debt-brake ceiling by 276.4 billion euro, including 179.4 billion euro for the Energy Stabilization Fund.
evidence.title: Abrechnung der grundgesetzlichen Regel zur Begrenzung der Neuverschuldung (Schuldenbremse) 2022
evidence.excerpt: The 2022 federal structural net borrowing reached 8.09 percent of GDP, exceeding the debt-brake ceiling by 276.4 billion euro, including 179.4 billion euro for the Energy Stabilization Fund.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official retrospective fiscal accounting with explicit 2022 figures.
evidence.period_fit: Retrospective accounting for the target year 2022.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Government-level fiscal record under Scholz, though partly driven by emergency authority and Bundestag declarations of exceptional conditions.
contrary_evidence: The same report notes the exceptional situation tied to the pandemic and the Russian invasion of Ukraine, which complicates a simple blame reading.

evidence.claim: At Meseberg the cabinet discussed securing energy supply, the national security strategy, and digital strategy, with Scholz emphasizing that the government had to ensure citizens and businesses could handle the economic and financial consequences; Habeck and Lindner took part in the joint press conference and external experts and business/agency leaders were invited to the meeting.
evidence.title: Closed Cabinet meeting at Schloss Meseberg
evidence.excerpt: At Meseberg the cabinet discussed securing energy supply, the national security strategy, and digital strategy, with Scholz emphasizing that the government had to ensure citizens and businesses could handle the economic and financial consequences; Habeck and Lindner took part in the joint press conference and external experts and business/agency leaders were invited to the meeting.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official government archive page documenting cabinet deliberation and participation by the relevant economic ministers and outside experts.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct Scholz-led cabinet process, though not a single-person economic appointment decision.
contrary_evidence: The source is process evidence, not an audit of policy quality or outcomes.

unresolved_gaps: No primary record of a Scholz-led command-and-control, custody, or safety reform in 2022.
The strongest direct evidence is signaling and procurement, not measured risk-reduction outcomes.
No private cabinet, NATO, or Russian-channel records showing the full decision chain behind caution, escalation limits, and ceasefire efforts.
No enacted 2022 Scholz-led federal police-oversight, complaint, or anti-racism reform was recovered.
The record is stronger on baseline freedoms, court protection, and limited reforms than on direct Scholz-led 2022 expansion of contestability.
Household-level distribution and long-run productivity effects remain thinner than the policy and macro response record.
Independent 2022 outcome data on take-up, distribution, and durability of the social measures is limited.
No direct, independently verified evidence of personal enrichment, family/business conflict, or nepotism was recovered.
The central Cum-Ex dispute still lacks the original transcript or decision PDF needed to resolve the truthfulness question cleanly.
Direct personnel, delegation, and implementation-discipline evidence is thinner than program, budget, procurement, and outcome evidence.
Some outcome indicators are partly inherited or shock-driven, so causal attribution for 2022 success remains mixed.
